name: Dark Yellow Green
lede: Dark Yellow Green is a dark, olive-leaning green, simply the plain words "dark" and "yellow green" combined; no catalog or dictionary in our sources files the name at all.

sections.title: A plain description, undocumented elsewhere
sections.body: The name is the plainest kind of compound: *dark* plus *yellow green*, describing the color directly rather than naming it after a place, person or material [1]. It does not appear in Ridgway's 1912 atlas, the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955, or Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary in our sources, and there is no separate "Yellow Green" entry to call its parent [1]. Who coined it, and when, is undocumented here [1]. Its nearest named neighbors on file are [[avocado]] and [[ugly-green]], both almost the same at 2.8 CIEDE2000 units, and the gem [[gem:peridot|peridot]], the closest colored stone [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this olive green, as photographed, in only 7 of 23,781 paintings, 0.03 percent, rarer than 77 percent of the named colors we track [3]. The earliest dated match is an 1890 Henri Moret landscape of Brittany; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. With so few matches, no century, painter or country stands out against the archive's own baseline [3].
